decisions.reason: Metro data centre connectivity runs on owned fibre, showed early adoption by data centres and financial hubs, and fits the high-bandwidth strategy, so the option keeps its value at low holding cost.
Optical spectrum services match the strategy of high-bandwidth, software-defined infrastructure and cost little to keep on the existing network while demand from hyperscalers and carriers develops.
A self-service number ordering portal supports the voice business and real-time provisioning at low marginal cost, though it could be folded into a broader portal.
Carrier pre-selection is a shrinking legacy service whose value is unlikely to grow, but it still runs cheaply on existing infrastructure, so it is kept for now with a high chance of withdrawal.
Direct voice connection services are core to enterprise voice and the ongoing shift to SIP, and they are cheap to maintain on the owned network.
